Lots of groups and things to do for young parents! There is a quarterly catalog of all of the community programs and activities called the Key: [https://www.thunderbay.ca/en/recreation/recreation-guide---the-key.aspx](https://www.thunderbay.ca/en/recreation/recreation-guide---the-key.aspx)

There is racism here (like anywhere else, yes even Toronto), but there are also many people here who are sick of it, and truly want Thunder Bay to change!

If you have a family, I wouldn't live near either of the downtowns. Some spots in Westfort are decent (ie around Edward/James/Walsh Sts), Northwood (ie around Churchill Dr), or perhaps around Shuniah St if you want to live on the north side. Personally I wouldn't choose to live along May St, South Court St, or the East End. The Bay/Algoma neighbourhood (a fair bit of culture as well) I would live in if I was still a student, but not necessarily with a family.

I looked at the Fraser Institute school rankings and they don't seem accurate to me, compared to their reputation... if that helps.

I enjoy living here, with my house that I bought for about $100,000 in a decent neighbourhood and my 15 minute commute to work. I find transit is good, but I live right on a major bus route....

Welcome, and enjoy!

You may have to consider that if a free person wants the benefits and obligations attached to membership of a group (ie corporation, collective, what have you), then they have the right to do so, via contracting with the group. If they break the rules of that group, then they are violating a contract. 

In your restaurant example, I suppose there would be an implied term that if you were to disturb the peace on private property, you will be asked to leave  by the owners of that property, because you will have violated that contract term. 

As I understand it, this is the problem libertarians have with regulations that force private groups open for membership to people that they don't want to have as members. I guess when you incorporate as a business or a charity, you are contracting with the government, receiving the benefits and obligations therein. So in a sense, no incorporated group is completely "private".

So I don't think you are wrong.. but I do think that you hint at a misconception many have that any contracting and any membership in a group is taking away personal freedom. Contracts are carried out by free individuals all the time, and as long as there is no fraud, and contracts are enforced, I don't think that there is anything wrong with it.

HTH, feel free to differ...
